featured_reviews.name: Praful Herode
featured_reviews.review_text: Had there been an unlike button or negative star marking I would have given him minus five stars . My son called him as the MCB tripped . Upon arriving he first scolded the watchman of our society , then came upstairs and did something & then started arguing with me and asking me questions about geysers - watts etc etc . He was the most arrogant person I’ve ever met - he behaved like a Mr Electician of India - finally we decided not to do the job with him -we asked for his visiting chargers and he charged us ₹1200 and did not even complete the work . Never ever call him for any work , there are better people than him . He did not even complete his work , left it undone .
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
At the very outset, when I received your call, you informed me that there was a short circuit at your residence and asked how long I would take to reach. I clearly informed you that I would arrive within 20–25 minutes, and I reached within the committed time.
Since you had not shared the complete address or flat number, I had to enquire with the watchman. As you were standing downstairs, the watchman identified you and pointed you out to me. However, before I could reach you, you attempted to switch ON the circuit breaker yourself. During this attempt, sparks were emitted, clearly indicating that the fault had not been cleared. I immediately intimated you that the short circuit needed to be rectified before restoring power.
Once inside the house, I enquired about what appliance was switched ON when the lights went off. You informed me that while switching ON the geyser, a loud sound occurred and the lights went off. Based on this, I began my inspection professionally and systematically.
I first checked the geyser plug point, which was found to be in proper condition. I then inspected the geyser and suspected an internal issue. Upon opening the distribution board, I found a major wiring fault.
The geyser requires 4mm or 6mm wiring, whereas two pieces of 2.5mm wire had been improperly used, which is unsafe and against standard practice. Due to this incorrect wiring, the wires were overheating, sticking to adjacent wires, and this directly caused the short circuit.
I rectified the immediate fault by separating the overheated wires and informed you that the circuit breaker installed was of low amperage, already burnt, and needed to be replaced with a higher-ampere MCB.
When you asked why this issue had occurred, I clearly explained that you were using an instant geyser, which must be operated by opening the water flow first and only then switching ON the power. Failing to do so can cause excessive heating and may even lead to serious hazards, as it is not a storage geyser.
Instead of understanding this safety concern, you responded rudely and arrogantly, stating “I am a doctor, don’t teach me,” along with several other disrespectful remarks, both from you and your son. Any technical explanation or safety guidance provided by me was taken as arrogance by you, and you became angry without any valid reason.
You then stated that you did not want the work to be continued and asked only for the charges incurred. I informed you that the total charges, including inspection and MCB replacement, would be ₹1500. When you insisted on only service charges, considering the time invested, fault detection, complete line inspection, and my 30 years of professional experience, I reasonably quoted ₹1200. And that is the reason why I had to leave the pending work and the board open just like that.
Despite this, you continued arguing and attempted to pressure and belittle me by repeatedly referring to your profession, which is completely irrelevant in a technical service matter. Charges are based on knowledge, experience, time, and risk involved, not on one’s designation.
By observing your behaviour, I genuinely began to question whether you are a doctor at all, and whether you behave in the same manner with your patients. It raises serious concerns about whether patients are treated with proper knowledge and professionalism. Such behaviour is risky, and people should think twice before visiting your clinic and do so strictly at their own risk.
Additionally, the review you have posted itself reflects carelessness, as even the spelling of the word “charges” is incorrect. Calling yourself a doctor while displaying such negligence and lack of basic professionalism further makes your claims highly doubtful.
Your conduct throughout the interaction was unwarranted, disrespectful, and unprofessional towards a technician who was performing his duty responsibly and honestly.
